company.name: Impossible Foods
company.shortDescription: Impossible Foods focuses on developing plant-based substitutes for meat, dairy, and fish products.
company.description:
Impossible Foods focuses on developing plant-based substitutes for meat, dairy, and fish products. It selects specific proteins and nutrients from greens, seeds, and grains to recreate the experience of meats and dairy products.

Founded by Patrick Brown and Monte Casino in 2011, Impossible Foods is headquartered in Redwood City, California.

aiResearchSummary.text: Impossible Foods is researching non-animal-based whole-cut food products that simulate aligned meat fibers and ground meat replicas that mimic fibrousness, heterogeneity, flavor, and color change. They develop methods and compositions for consumables, including plant based meat substitutes, cheese replicas from non-dairy milks, and non-animal meat replicas with heme-containing proteins, alongside protein purification, reductant treatment methods, flavor and aroma modulation, and secretion of heme-containing polypeptides. These efforts span plant-based meat, dairy, and processing technologies.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Series H round raised $500,000,000, or 26.37% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.
caveats: Crunchbase reports 12 rounds but provides 10 detailed rows.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $166,826,461 to $7,000,000,000, a 41.96x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 38 (-6 over 90 days) and market heat at 14 (-14).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
